title: LiveMem: Maintaining Memory State Continuity in Long-Running LLM Inference
summary: LiveMem is a method for maintaining memory state continuity in long-running LLM inference, addressing the issue of context retention and retrieval in interactive systems. It formulates the problem as a sequence of interactions and proposes a solution based on persistent state management.
why_builders_care: Builders can use LiveMem to develop more effective and efficient interactive AI systems that can handle long-running conversations and tasks.

title: lamhotsiagian/llm-system-design
summary: This repository provides a production-grade LLM system design platform, featuring a pure-Python LLM serving, RAG, routing, safety, and agent control plane, along with a LangChain + Streamlit UI and local Ollama models.
why_builders_care: Builders can leverage this platform to design and deploy their own LLM systems, integrating various components and tools for efficient and safe operation.

title: GradCuit: Credit-Assigned Gradient Flow Enables Robust and Interpretable Test-Time Latent Reasoning
summary: GradCuit is a method for optimizing instance-specific continuous states at test time, enabling robust and interpretable latent reasoning in large language models. It connects these states to the reasoning trajectory through decoded tokens.
why_builders_care: Builders can apply GradCuit to improve the performance and interpretability of their LLMs, especially in tasks requiring test-time adaptation and reasoning.

title: A Taxonomy of Cognitive Capability Gaps in Generative and Agentic AI
summary: This paper presents a taxonomy of cognitive capability gaps in generative and agentic AI, highlighting the limitations and challenges of current AI systems in areas such as sustained reasoning, adaptive behavior, and self-regulation.
why_builders_care: Builders can use this taxonomy to identify and address the cognitive gaps in their AI systems, guiding the development of more advanced and capable AI models.

title: Stateless MCP has recaptured my interest (and inspired mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp)
summary: This article discusses the recent developments in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), particularly the introduction of stateless MCP, and its potential applications and implications for AI agents and systems.
why_builders_care: Builders can explore the possibilities of stateless MCP and its integration with various tools and frameworks, such as mcp-explorer and datasette-mcp, to enhance their AI systems.

title: artbyjazi/autoclip
summary: Autoclip is an open-source, local-first AI video clipper that can process long videos and produce caption-burned, speaker-tracked clips in a 9:16 format, using Whisper and Ollama.
why_builders_care: Builders can utilize Autoclip to develop their own video processing and clipping tools, leveraging the power of AI for efficient and accurate video analysis.

title: GPT-5.6 fuses frontier intelligence with frontier efficiency
summary: This article discusses the recent release of GPT-5.6, which combines advanced intelligence and efficiency, enabling more effective and productive AI applications and workflows.
why_builders_care: Builders can take advantage of GPT-5.6 to develop more powerful and efficient AI systems, integrating the latest advancements in language models and agent technologies.

title: Black Forest Labs FLUX 3 - Multimodal Flow Models
summary: FLUX 3 is a multimodal flow model that outperforms other models like Seedance 2.0, Gemini Omni, and Grok Imagine, and also features a video-action robotics model called FLUX-mimic.
why_builders_care: Builders can explore the capabilities of FLUX 3 and its applications in multimodal processing and robotics, potentially integrating it into their own AI projects.

title: juxhinr/bindwidth
summary: Bindwidth is an evidence-aware on-prem LLM inference sizing and TCO calculator, helping builders to optimize their AI systems for better performance and cost-effectiveness.
why_builders_care: Builders can use Bindwidth to calculate the optimal sizing and cost of their LLM inference workloads, ensuring efficient and scalable AI operations.

title: CoWAM: Coordination Contracts for Selective Policy Intervention with WAMs
summary: CoWAM is a method for selective policy intervention in World Action Models (WAMs), enabling more effective and efficient decision-making in complex environments.
why_builders_care: Builders can apply CoWAM to improve the performance and adaptability of their AI systems, particularly in tasks requiring coordinated action and policy intervention.
